evals.prompt: I've got an extract from our GP diabetes registry at evals/files/diabetes_registry_extract.csv. We want to use it to estimate diabetes incidence trends by year, 2005 to 2020, across the 8 practices for a paper. Can you check the data quality and tell me whether it's usable for that? Columns are patient_id, practice_id, sex, birth_date, registration_date, diagnosis_date, dm_type (T1 / T2 / Unspecified / Proxy, where Proxy means a 'seen in diabetic clinic' type code), hba1c_mmol_mol, bmi, insulin_rx, oad_rx, death_date. Write the assessment up as a markdown report I can share with the study team.
evals.expected_output: A markdown data quality report that leads with a fitness-for-use verdict for the incidence-trend question, reports a record-level perfect-record score with an interval over named critical fields, ranks error types, detects the 2006-04-01 date spike, the practice-level variation (P04 proxy coding drift from 2017, P07 HbA1c missingness), duplicates, invalid sex codes, Type 1 without insulin, death before diagnosis, placeholder values (999 HbA1c, -1 BMI), recommends tiered definitions / sensitivity analysis across dm_type categories, distinguishes fix-at-source from cleaning, and lists limitations (accuracy unmeasured, pedigree unknowns).
expectations: The report opens with an explicit fitness-for-use verdict (fit / fit with caveats / not fit) tied to the stated incidence-trend question
A record-level perfect-record (or equivalent all-critical-fields-correct) percentage is reported with a confidence interval and compared against an explicit acceptance bar
The critical data elements used for scoring are listed explicitly
The 2006-04-01 diagnosis-date spike is detected and interpreted as probable retrospective or batch entry

A per-practice defect or error rate covering several fields (not just one column's missingness) is tabulated or charted with some notion of expected variation (control or funnel limits, or a comparison to the overall rate), and P04 and P07 are singled out as outliers
The shift of practice P04 towards Proxy dm_type codes from 2017 onwards is detected and flagged as a recording-practice artefact (drift)
Duplicate patient_id records are counted
Non-standard sex codes (Female, Male, U, f) and placeholder values (999 in hba1c, -1 in bmi) are identified rather than treated as valid data
Cross-field inconsistencies are reported: Type 1 patients with no insulin and death dates before diagnosis dates
The report recommends running the incidence estimate under tiered or alternative case definitions (e.g. excluding Proxy/Unspecified) and reporting the spread
Error types are ranked (Pareto-style) and the top ones are traced to a likely origin in the data-creating process
Recommendations distinguish fixing at the source / prevention from one-off cleaning and propose ongoing monitoring
A limitations section states what could not be assessed (e.g. accuracy against a reference, pedigree unknowns)

evals.prompt: Here's evals/files/hba1c_lab_results.csv, pulled from the lab information system feeds of our four sites (columns: patient_id, site, test_date, analyte, value, unit, result_entered_date). I need the proportion of patients with HbA1c under 53 mmol/mol per site per quarter for a quality dashboard. Before I build it, can you sanity-check the data for me and tell me if there's anything I should worry about?
evals.expected_output: An assessment that discovers Site_C's values are on a different scale (percent NGSP rather than mmol/mol despite the unit column), Site_D's upward shift from July 2024 (analyser change), zero placeholder values, duplicated result rows and Site_B's long entry lag; concludes the data is not fit for the <53 mmol/mol metric without unit harmonisation and investigation of Site_D; raises measurement-system / pedigree questions; and gives a verdict rather than only a list.
expectations: The response identifies that Site_C's values are on a different scale (consistent with percent rather than mmol/mol) despite the unit column saying mmol/mol
The response identifies the upward shift in Site_D values from around July 2024 and suggests a measurement-system cause (analyser or method change) to investigate
Zero values are flagged as placeholders or implausible rather than counted as controlled HbA1c
Duplicate result rows are counted
Entry lag (result_entered_date minus test_date) is examined and Site_B's long lag is reported as a timeliness problem
The response gives an explicit verdict that the data is not fit for the <53 mmol/mol dashboard metric as-is, and names what must happen first (unit harmonisation, Site_D investigation)
The response quantifies the impact on the metric (e.g. Site_C would appear ~100% controlled) rather than only listing issues
The response asks or recommends pedigree / measurement-system questions (which analyser, which unit convention, who enters results) rather than only cleaning the file
Variation across sites is shown explicitly (per-site summary), not only pooled statistics

evals.prompt: Our pharmacovigilance team receives a monthly case-listing feed from a vendor, about 5,000 rows each month with case_id, receipt_date, product, event_term (MedDRA PT), seriousness, country, reporter_type, outcome. Nobody formally checks it before it goes into signal detection. Can you design a data quality check and monitoring process for this feed that the team can actually run every month? We're statisticians, not data engineers.
evals.expected_output: A practical measurement system: define the data customer (signal detection) and 10-15 critical elements with error definitions; a first Friday Afternoon Measurement style manual review of the last 100 cases to get a perfect-record baseline; pedigree questions for the vendor; automated monthly rules with a record-level perfect-record rate charted over time with control limits (p-chart); checkpoints that hold the feed when limits are breached; feedback to the vendor; ownership; re-evaluation when the feed's use changes; cost framed via rule of ten.
expectations: The plan names signal detection as the data customer and derives critical data elements and error definitions from what signal detection needs
The plan includes an initial manual review of a recent sample of records (e.g. last 100 cases) producing a record-level perfect-record percentage baseline
The plan includes a list of pedigree / provenance questions to ask the vendor (how cases are collected, coded, deduplicated, what is excluded, MedDRA version, timeliness)
The plan specifies concrete automated monthly checks per field (completeness, allowed values, date plausibility, duplicates, cross-field consistency such as seriousness vs outcome)
The plan tracks the record-level perfect-record rate over time on a control chart with limits and defines what happens when a point is out of control
The plan includes a checkpoint or gate that stops or quarantines the feed from entering signal detection when quality breaches the agreed standard
The plan assigns ownership and a feedback loop to the vendor / data creators, emphasising prevention at source over repeated cleaning
The plan states an explicit acceptance standard (e.g. percentage of perfect records) and justifies it

The plan is self-contained (every script or template it relies on is included in the deliverable, nothing imported from an external path), runnable with spreadsheet-level or single-script tooling, and states a monthly routine with roles and a total person-hours estimate under about three hours
The plan includes a periodic accuracy check against an independent reference (e.g. tracing a sample of cases back to the safety database), since automated rules cannot measure accuracy
